match.reason: No bank point teaches the scalar (dot) product or the formula cos θ = a·b ÷ (|a||b|) for the angle between vectors. The closest matches cover vectors in physics or the cosine rule for triangles, which are related but different ideas.

draft.title: Angles between vectors
card: The scalar product of a = a1i + a2j + a3k and b = b1i + b2j + b3k is a·b = a1b1 + a2b2 + a3b3. It is also a·b = |a||b| cos θ, where θ is the angle between them.
Put the two together: cos θ = (a·b) ÷ (|a||b|). Find the scalar product, find both lengths, divide, then use inverse cosine.
If a·b = 0, then cos θ = 0, so θ = 90°. Two non-zero vectors with a·b = 0 are perpendicular.
Example: a = i + 2j + 2k and b = 2i − j + 2k. a·b = 2 − 2 + 4 = 4. |a| = 3 and |b| = 3. So cos θ = 4/9 and θ ≈ 63.6°.
draft.remember: cos θ = a·b ÷ (|a||b|), and a·b = 0 means the vectors are perpendicular.

a.q: For a = 2i + j − k and b = i − 3j + k, what does a·b show?
opts: a·b = −2, so the angle is obtuse
a·b = 2, so the angle is acute
a·b = −2, so the angle is acute
a.why: a·b = 2 × 1 + 1 × (−3) + (−1) × 1 = 2 − 3 − 1 = −2. Since |a| and |b| are positive, cos θ is negative, so θ is obtuse. A negative scalar product does not mean an acute angle.
a.clue: Multiply matching components, then add them.

b.q: For which value of m are p = 2i + mj + k and q = i − 2j + 4k perpendicular?
b.why: p·q = 2 − 2m + 4 = 6 − 2m. Perpendicular means p·q = 0, so m = 3. Checking: 2 − 6 + 4 = 0. The value m = −3 comes from a sign slip, as it gives 6 + 6 = 12.
b.clue: Set the scalar product equal to zero and solve for m.

a.best: a·b = −2, so the angle is obtuse

check.summary: No problems found. The card's example and both questions check out: a·b = −2 gives an obtuse angle, and m = 3 makes p and q perpendicular.

final.title: Angles between vectors
card: The scalar product of \(a = a_{1}i + a_{2}j + a_{3}k\) and \(b = b_{1}i + b_{2}j + b_{3}k\) is \(a \cdot b = a_{1}b_{1} + a_{2}b_{2} + a_{3}b_{3}\). It is also \(a \cdot b = |a||b| \cos \theta\), where \(\theta\) is the angle between them.
Put the two together: \(\cos \theta = \frac{a \cdot b}{|a||b|}\). Find the scalar product, find both lengths, divide, then use inverse cosine.
If \(a \cdot b = 0\), then \(\cos \theta = 0\), so \(\theta = 90^{\circ}\). Two non-zero vectors with \(a \cdot b = 0\) are perpendicular.
Example: \(a = i + 2j + 2k\) and \(b = 2i - j + 2k\). \(a \cdot b = 2 - 2 + 4 = 4\). \(|a| = 3\) and \(|b| = 3\). So \(\cos \theta = \frac{4}{9}\) and \(\theta \approx 63.6^{\circ}\).
final.remember: \(\cos \theta = \frac{a \cdot b}{|a||b|}\), and \(a \cdot b = 0\) means the vectors are perpendicular.

a.q: For \(a = 2i + j - k\) and \(b = i - 3j + k\), what does \(a \cdot b\) show?
opts: \(a \cdot b = -2\), so the angle is obtuse
\(a \cdot b = 2\), so the angle is acute
\(a \cdot b = -2\), so the angle is acute
a.why: \(a \cdot b = 2 \times 1 + 1 \times (-3) + (-1) \times 1\), which is \(2 - 3 - 1 = -2\). Since \(|a|\) and \(|b|\) are positive, \(\cos \theta\) is negative, so \(\theta\) is obtuse. A negative scalar product does not mean an acute angle.
a.clue: Multiply matching components, then add them.

b.q: For which value of \(m\) are \(p = 2i + mj + k\) and \(q = i - 2j + 4k\) perpendicular?
b.why: \(p \cdot q = 2 - 2m + 4 = 6 - 2m\). Perpendicular means \(p \cdot q = 0\), so \(m = 3\). Checking: \(2 - 6 + 4 = 0\). The value \(m = -3\) comes from a sign slip, as it gives \(6 + 6 = 12\).
b.clue: Set the scalar product equal to zero and solve for \(m\).
